start_enabled.description: Start daemonlogger automatically at boot. Set to false to install the package without activating the daemon.

daemon_user.description: System user account the daemon drops privileges to after opening the raw capture socket. Must have write access to log_dir.

daemon_group.description: System group the daemon drops privileges to after opening the raw capture socket.

interface.description: Network interface to capture packets from (e.g. eth0, ens3, bond0). The interface must be up before the daemon starts.

tap_interface.description: Optional soft-tap output interface. A verbatim copy of each captured packet is injected here in addition to being logged. Leave empty to disable.

log_dir.description: Directory where pcap capture files are written. Must exist and be writable by daemon_user before the daemon starts.

log_prefix.description: Filename prefix for pcap log files. A Unix timestamp suffix is appended automatically (e.g. capture.1718000000.pcap).

snaplen.description: Per-packet snapshot length in bytes. 1514 captures the full payload of a standard 1500-byte MTU Ethernet frame. Increase to 9014 for jumbo frames.

rollover_size.description: Maximum pcap file size in bytes before rotating to a new file. 134217728 = 128 MiB. Set to 0 to disable size-based rotation.

rollover_time.description: Maximum pcap file age in seconds before rotating to a new file. 3600 = 1 hour. Set to 0 to disable time-based rotation.

max_files.description: Maximum number of pcap files to keep on disk. The oldest file is deleted when this limit is reached. 0 means unlimited — manage retention externally via logrotate or cron.

pid_file.description: Absolute path to the PID file. The parent directory must exist and be writable by daemon_user before the daemon starts.

verbose.description: Enable verbose debug output to syslog. Useful for initial setup and troubleshooting; disable in production to avoid log noise.

bpf_rules.description: List of Berkeley Packet Filter rule atoms. They are OR-combined into a single BPF expression passed to libpcap. An empty list captures all traffic on the interface. See pcap-filter(7) for syntax.

expr.description: BPF filter atom or sub-expression (e.g. 'port 443', 'not host 10.0.0.1', 'tcp and portrange 8000-9000').

description.description: Human-readable label for this rule, rendered as a comment above the generated BPF_FILTER line.

extra_args.description: Additional command-line flags passed verbatim to daemonlogger. Use only for options not exposed as dedicated variables above.
